sentences.text:
The instant revision petition is moved against the judgment of conviction and order of sentence
dated 21.09.2002 passed by learned Acjm, No.2, Chittorgarh so also judgment dated 18.11.2004
whereby judgment of learned trial court was affirmed.
2.  Briefly stated facts of the case are that the food inspector Mr. RS Pandey on 11.08.1887 spotted the petitioner while he was carrying milk with him.
Samples were taken and sent to the laboratory.
The complaint came to be submitted under Section 7/16 of the Prevention of Food Adulteration Act on the ground of report of adulteration in the food.
The complaint came to be submitted on 26.04.1988.
On 19.11.1988, an application was preferred on behalf of the petitioner under Section 13(2) of PF Act seeking re-analysis of the samples by the central laboratory.
The said application was allowed and vide 12.12.1988 learned trial court directed to send the sample to central laboratory.
Samples [2025:RJ-JD:24812] (2 of 3) [CRLR-880/2004] were received by CFSL on 21.12.1988.
It was examined and then report dated 16.01.1989 was received.

Based on the affirmation of adulteration by the central laboratory as well as the report of HLA regarding adulteration of milk the petitioner was convicted and sentenced the appeal preferred by him has also been dismissed, hence this revision petition.

Naru vs State (2025:Rj-Jd:24812) on 21 May, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/180944853/
1 3.

The core issue available in this revision petition would be that sample of milk was taken on 11.08.1987 and it was sent to central laboratory on 12.12.1988 and received on 21.12.1988 and till that time the commodity which is a perishable item must have been deteriorated which is a persumable fact.
Certainly milk is a perishable item and it cannot be preserved even after adulteration of preservatives for more than six months.
Reliance can be placed on the judgment passed by Hon'ble Supreme Court in Girishbhai Dahyabhai Shah Vs. C.C. Jani and Anr. (2009) 15 SCC 64.

entities.text: Girishbhai Dahyabhai Shah Vs. C.C. Jani and Anr. (2009) 15 SCC 64
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Since the petitioner had a right to seek re-analysis of the sample and it was not sent to the central laboratory promptly, as a consequence of which, its content had deteriorated, therefore, the report of central laboratory cannot be taken as a piece of evidence to sustain conviction of accused under Section 7 r/w 16 of Food Adulteration Act.
Both the Courts have failed to notice the above significant fact and root of the case.
4. In view of the above, the instant revision petition succeeds and is hereby allowed.
5. The judgment of conviction dated 07.05.2004 passed by learned ACJM, No.2, Chittorgarh and order dated 18.11.2004 passed by learned Addl.
Sessions Judge, No.1, Chittorgarh are hereby quashed and set aside.

The petitioner is exonerated from [2025:RJ-JD:24812] (3 of 3)
[CRLR-880/2004] the charges.
His bail bonds are discharged.
He is on bail.
He need not surrender before the Court.
6. Record be send back forthwith.

(FARJAND ALI),J 6-chhavi/-
